Radiology Division | Academic Medical Centre | 05 Feb 2025 | Protocol: Multiparametric MRI Prostate

Clinical Context: Assessment of elevated prostate-specific antigen (4.8 ng/mL) coupled with a previously negative biopsy screen.

OBSERVATIONS: The organ encompasses a total capacity of 68.0 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a discrete region of profound hypointensity, roughly 18 mm in diameter, located in the mid-gland right peripheral zone. Diffusion-weighted imaging confirms restricted water motion with matching low apparent diffusion coefficient values. Post-contrast dynamics show prompt, localized enhancement compared to adjacent tissue. Capsular integrity remains intact without seminal vesicle involvement; adjacent pelvic structures appear normal.

CONCLUSION: PI-RADS 4 classification for the right peripheral zone mid-gland focus. PSAD 0.07 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.800129.

previous_notes.author: Dr. F. de Boer (GP)
previous_notes.text: During a June 2023 review, an initial prostate-specific antigen reading of 3.5 ng/mL triggered a repeat test alongside a reassuring digital rectal assessment. Following those earlier negative biopsy outcomes, the case was forwarded to the urology outpatient department for additional scrutiny.
